region: Burdett · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Chardonnay is where Osmote began. Ben Riccardi, a Finger Lakes native and Cornell-trained winemaker who worked harvests in France, New Zealand and Sonoma and later ran City Winery’s Manhattan program, made his first vintage in 2014: about 200 cases of Seneca Lake Chardonnay. His 2017 went on to win Best Oaked Chardonnay at the New York Wine & Food Classic. He and his wife, Britt, now farm 31 acres on the southeast shore of Seneca Lake in Burdett, where the winery has its own home.

Riccardi buys Chardonnay from growers around Seneca Lake and works with as little intervention as possible. The 2024 was fermented in barrel with wild yeasts and finished at a moderate 12.5% alcohol, typical of his cool-climate, lightly extracted style. Every Osmote wine has been naturally fermented since the first vintage, with minimal added sulfur. The Seneca Lake Chardonnay is also the one Osmote wine that travels abroad, poured at restaurants in Tokyo including the New York Grill at the Park Hyatt.

Jamie Goode rated the 2024 93 points, describing pear and peach with spicy citrus and a mealy richness, balanced and complex. Cream and peach notes, with a warm frame of French oak, point to the same generous but fresh style. Goode tasted it in 2026 alongside Osmote’s Riesling, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Franc, made since the move into the winery’s own facility.
